examples.label: Set the node id to attack

notes: CVE-2018-7602 is authenticated - you need a live session cookie and the target node id, so it's a post-login escalation, not an entry point.
name: Drupalgeddon3 - Authenticated RCE (Metasploit)
description: CVE-2018-7602 authenticated RCE. Requires a valid Drupal session cookie and a node id; set rhosts/vhost/drupal_session/drupal_node/lhost then exploit.

defense.why_it_works: Drupalgeddon3 (CVE-2018-7602) is an authenticated RCE exploiting insufficient sanitization of the destination parameter in node deletion form actions. Any authenticated user with node deletion permission can trigger it.
defense.prerequisites: Any authenticated Drupal user session. Drupal 7.x < 7.59 or 8.x < 8.5.3.
defense.impact: Authenticated RCE as www-data. Meterpreter session enabling full server control and credential harvesting.
defense.detection: Authenticated request to node deletion endpoint with exploit payload in destination parameter. Metasploit User-Agent in HTTP headers. Outbound TCP from web server to attacker IP.
defense.artifacts: Web server access log (POST to node delete with malicious destination) | Meterpreter network session in SIEM | Drupal watchdog log (node delete action)
defense.prevention: Update to Drupal 7.59 / 8.5.3 or later. Restrict user permissions -- node deletion for admins only. WAF signatures for CVE-2018-7602.
defense.misconfiguration: Drupal running unpatched with authenticated users able to trigger the vulnerable node deletion handler.
defense.secure_config:
drush pm-update
# Restrict node deletion role assignment
# WAF: block exploit pattern in destination parameter
